extracted.intended_audience: individual investors and members of the public who want to submit comments on SEC rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on how members of the public (especially individual investors) can submit comments to the SEC, covering available submission channels, required filing identifiers, acceptable file formats, privacy cautions, and the SEC's public posting/deduplication practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Comment Form
rubrics_metrics.description: "Submit a Comment" link on the rule/release page; attachments permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Submit a Comment' link on the specific rule or release page to submit electronically. Attachments are permitted via the online form, but use standard document formats (see Accepted file formats) and avoid HTML or executable attachment types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Email to rule-comments@sec.gov; include File Number (e.g., S7-, SR-, PCAOB-, 4-) in subject line. Accepted formats: PDF, Word, plain text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting by email, put the File Number in the subject line so the SEC can associate your comment with the correct docket. Attach files in accepted formats (PDF, Word, plain text) and avoid disallowed/unsupported types such as HTML, GIF, TIFF, PIF, ZIP, and EXE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper Mail submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail to: Secretary, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090, with the File Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the applicable File Number on mailed comments to ensure proper docketing. The SEC converts paper comments to PDF and posts them online, so mailed submissions will become part of the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback Flyer / Specialized webforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback Flyer (when available) — specialized webforms designed for individual investors with targeted questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a feedback flyer is available for a rulemaking, use the targeted webform; these ask focused questions intended to capture individual investor perspectives and may be simpler than a full comment letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC accepts comment letters in PDF format and other standard document types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred/explicitly accepted formats include PDF, Microsoft Word, and plain text. Use common, non-executable document types to ensure your submission can be processed and posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid certain attachment types
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid attachments in HTML or executable formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically avoid submitting attachments in HTML, GIF, TIFF, PIF, ZIP, EXE and other executable or nonstandard container types, as these may not be accepted or may not process/convert properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include personally identifiable information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include personal identifiable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the SEC makes all comments available to the public and posts them online, omit personal identifiers (such as SSNs, account numbers, personal contact information) to protect privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and deduplication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "All comments will be made available to the public." When identical submissions arrive, only the first is published with a count of duplicates — meaning template campaigns are deduplicated by design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that your comment will become part of the public record. Identical or template-based campaign submissions may be consolidated (only the first posted with a duplicate count), so provide unique content if you want an individually posted comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Number requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the File Number (e.g., S7-, SR-, PCAOB-, 4-) in email subject or on mailed submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the File Number is necessary for the SEC to associate your comment with the correct rulemaking or release; omitting it may delay or misfile your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult SEC investor bulletin for substantive guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: SEC publishes an investor bulletin 'Suggestions for How Individual Investors Can Comment on SEC Rulemaking' with substantive guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the SEC's investor bulletin for more detailed recommendations on what to say and how to structure substantive comments if you are an individual investor seeking guidance beyond procedural submission steps.
